why: #396. Filed as a same-file `IMPLEMENTS` resolution defect ("a supertype declared in the same file as its subtype produces no edge") — but `_resolve_type`'s same-package guess makes no distinction between same-file and same-package-different-file, and there was never a code path matching that description. What actually reproduces the filed repro is a `tree-sitter-kotlin` 1.1.0 scanner ambiguity: a body that opens and closes on one line — `interface Iface { fun f() }` here, and `class B { fun f() {} }` or `interface I { fun f(): Unit }` just as well — produces an `ERROR` that loses every declaration after it, not just the `IMPLEMENTS` edge. Every prior Kotlin corpus case put the supertype in a separate file or used multi-line bodies, so nothing exercised this shape, and it looked like a resolution-logic gap rather than a parser one. `_recover_collapsed_parse` detects the collapse (only when the initial parse already contains an `ERROR` — a cleanly-parsing file takes none of this path) and moves the body's closing brace onto its own line before re-parsing. It tries only brace pairs that overlap an `ERROR`, keeps a split only when it strictly shrinks the total `ERROR` span, and uses the result only when it parses cleanly. A line-remap table then reports the original file's line numbers, not the modified buffer's.
